material.narrative: [dequeue-receive-is-serialized: pass] The exact extracted head reaches at most one concurrent recv while the base reaches two, so the intended serialization is effective. [lock-wait-consumes-caller-timeout-budget: fail] With an 80 ms lock hold and a 100 ms caller timeout, the head takes 180.21 ms because recv receives a fresh timeout after lock acquisition. The added test does not cover the total deadline. [uncontended-overhead-remains-sub-microsecond: pass] The median rises from 172.4 ns to 397.2 ns; the relative ratio is large but the absolute increase remains below one microsecond.

observations.conclusion: The exact extracted head reaches at most one concurrent recv while the base reaches two, so the intended serialization is effective.
observations.question: Does the new lock prevent concurrent reader-cursor/socket receives?

observations.conclusion: With an 80 ms lock hold and a 100 ms caller timeout, the head takes 180.21 ms because recv receives a fresh timeout after lock acquisition. The added test does not cover the total deadline.
counterevidence: The serialization race itself is fixed.
observations.question: Does lock acquisition consume the same end-to-end timeout budget as recv?

observations.conclusion: The median rises from 172.4 ns to 397.2 ns; the relative ratio is large but the absolute increase remains below one microsecond.
observations.question: Is the uncontended absolute lock overhead small enough to retain the approach?
